prompt: Why does the lesson say every yes is also a no?

choices.text: Because the CEO expects to hear no
choices.why: Nothing suggests that.

choices.text: Because a yes is always followed by a refusal later
choices.why: Not always, and not the mechanism the lesson describes.

choices.text: It spends capacity promised elsewhere
choices.why: Right: said silently to whoever loses, who finds out later.

choices.text: Because people who ask for things tend to forget them later
choices.why: Not the argument; the cost falls on other work, not on memory.

prompt: Five engineers, twelve working days each. How many engineer-days does the checkout team have before Black Friday?
With 55 engineer-days already committed and flash deals estimated at 30, how many engineer-days over capacity would a yes put the team?
Why is "we'll do our best" the worst answer to Otávio, by the lesson?

choices.text: It reveals the team's capacity to a competitor
choices.why: Not a concern in the lesson.

choices.text: He plans on it, and the failure shows up when it is too late to act
choices.why: Right: a clear no on 10 November leaves seventeen days; a failed "we'll try" on the 26th leaves none.

choices.text: It commits the team to working weekends
choices.why: It commits to nothing, which is the problem.

choices.text: It sounds unprofessional to a CEO
choices.why: Tone is not the problem.

prompt: Put the parts of a good no in order.
Why does the lesson drop "unfortunately" and "it might be difficult" from a no?

choices.text: They are too informal for a message to the CEO of the company
choices.why: Formality is not the issue.

choices.text: They make the no unclear, and it is heard as yes
choices.why: Right: softening words do not make a no kinder.

choices.text: They admit fault, which is a legal risk
choices.why: That is lesson 3's point about apologies to clients, not this one.

choices.text: They waste words, and economy is the main rule
choices.why: Economy matters, but the danger named is being misheard.

prompt: Lívia answered Otávio "Give me until tomorrow at 10:00". Why does the lesson count that as a good first answer?

choices.text: A considered no is worth more than an instant one
choices.why: Right: with a time to come back, it is not an evasion.

choices.text: It delays the conversation until he forgets
choices.why: She came back at 10:00 with the full answer.

choices.text: CEOs prefer answers in writing the next day
choices.why: Not the reason given.

choices.text: It lets her check with Bruna whether to say yes after all
choices.why: She did check the alternative with Bruna, but the reason is the value of a considered answer.

prompt: Which reason fits Otávio's unit, by the lesson?

choices.text: The reservation logic needs distributed locking across the checkout nodes
choices.why: Bottom rung of the ladder; he decides higher up.

choices.text: The team is tired after a long year
choices.why: Possibly true, and not the reason that decides this.

choices.text: It would put Black Friday itself at risk, as 6 March did
choices.why: Right: risk to the business, and an outage he remembers.

choices.text: Flash deals are a bad idea in general
choices.why: An opinion, and the lesson treats the request as reasonable.

prompt: Match each kind of alternative to its flash-deal version.

pairs.right: a countdown banner without reserved stock
a timed offer from marketing's email tool
the substitution flow moves to February

right_distractors: a bigger server for Black Friday

prompt: Why does the lesson call "yes, if" often the most useful alternative?
hint: Who is entitled to the trade-off?

choices.text: It is the cheapest alternative to build
choices.why: It is not an alternative to build; it is a trade.

choices.text: It always ends with the team doing less work
choices.why: It may end with more work, if the trade is accepted.

choices.text: It sounds like a yes, so nobody is upset
choices.why: Its value is honesty about the cost, not sounding nice.

choices.text: It hands the trade to the person entitled to it
choices.why: Right: Otávio can trade the substitution flow; Lívia cannot decide that for him.

prompt: Which parts of Otávio's request carried most of the visible effect for little cost? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Stock reserved for whoever adds the item first
choices.why: That is most of the risk and most of the cost.

choices.text: The one-hour discount
choices.why: Yes: the promotions engine already supports it.

choices.text: The countdown on the home screen
choices.why: Yes: what customers see.

prompt: Lívia offers the banner without checking with Bruna, "to soften the no". What does the lesson say?
hint: Would you be glad to be held to it?

choices.text: Fine, since that is what alternatives exist for: softening a refusal
choices.why: They exist to serve the need.

choices.text: Bruna should only be asked after Otávio has accepted the banner offer
choices.why: Then the offer may be one the team cannot keep.

choices.text: An alternative not meant to be delivered is worse than a plain no
choices.why: Right: offer only what you would be glad to be held to.

choices.text: Fine, if the banner is cheaper than the original request
choices.why: Cheap is not the test; being real is.

prompt: Lívia ends her options to Otávio with "It's your call." What does that do, by the lesson?

choices.text: It shifts the blame to him if Black Friday fails
choices.why: Not the purpose; the trade-off is his by right.

choices.text: It makes him somebody consulted, not refused
choices.why: Right: and it is the honest end of the sentence.

choices.text: It ends the meeting
choices.why: It opens the decision.

choices.text: It gives up her recommendation
choices.why: She recommended the second option in the same breath.

prompt: After the boss chooses the option you argued against, which belong to committing? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Put the disagreement on the record, briefly
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Keep raising it at every meeting until it is reversed
choices.why: That is relitigating.

choices.text: Bring new evidence if it arrives, without relitigating
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Do the work properly
choices.why: Yes: a half-hearted delivery is sabotage with an excuse.

prompt: Otávio asks Lívia to ship the flash-deal change without the security review "just this once". What does the lesson say?

choices.text: Disagree, put it on the record, and commit, as with any decision he makes
choices.why: That covers choices between legitimate options; this is not one.

choices.text: Ship it quietly and run the review afterwards
choices.why: That skips the review and hides it.

choices.text: Say no plainly, in writing, and take it to whoever the company names
choices.why: Right: if he will not change his mind.

choices.text: Comply, since as CEO he owns the risk and has said it is only this once
choices.why: Committing to an unsafe request is not loyalty.

prompt: In the note declining a design review by Friday, what does Lívia offer?

choices.text: Nothing; a no needs no alternative between peers
choices.why: Every no in the lesson carries one.

choices.text: Tuesday the 1st, or Bruna this week
choices.why: Right: not now, or not me, and the reader chooses.

choices.text: A quick look on Friday, without a proper review
choices.why: She declines exactly that.

choices.text: A template so they can review their own design
choices.why: Not in the note.

prompt: Match each weakening phrase to what the lesson writes instead.

pairs.left: "Unfortunately, I'm afraid it might be difficult to…"

pairs.right: a date you will keep, or no

pairs.left: "It's not really a priority right now"

prompt: In the no to Tânia, why is the refusal framed around the company's plan rather than a team?

choices.text: So the client cannot negotiate with the team directly
choices.why: A side effect at most; not the reason.

choices.text: Internal teams are not the client's business
choices.why: Right: one voice, no internal names, no internal disagreements.

choices.text: To hide that the reporting team is understaffed and behind on everything
choices.why: Nothing suggests that; the reason is how a client should be written to.

choices.text: Because Tânia asked to speak to Otávio
choices.why: She did not.

prompt: Renata asks Bruna's team for a gift-wrapping option at checkout by Black Friday. Which reply has the five parts?

choices.text: "Unfortunately we're very busy, but we'll try our best to fit it in."
choices.why: A vague yes: no need, no reason, no door.

choices.text: "You want gifts to feel easy that day. Not by the 27th: it risks the sale itself. A gift note on the order works now. The rest fits January if it beats substitutions."
choices.why: Right: all five, in order.

choices.text: "Gift wrapping is a bad idea for a grocery app, so we will not be doing it."
choices.why: An opinion as a reason, and no alternative.

choices.text: "No. Checkout is frozen until December."
choices.why: A no and a reason, and nothing else.
